sections.content: Simple content that doesn't require much thinking, just show up to class and pay attention and you should do well in the exams.
sections.teaching: Super chill dude who talks at a very slow pace. He uses slides to teach every lesson but doesn't just read off of it. Explains everything in very simple terms and likes to tell jokes. He gives plenty of opportunities for everyone in the class to participate, which is good because participation is also graded.
sections.grading: Super good grading and very lenient, however this was his first semester teaching so I suspect he may become less lenient in the future.
sections.workload: There is a mid-term and final exam, both of which includes MCQs and short answer questions. Questions can be quite tricky if you do not understand the content well or pay attention in class. There is also some readings to do which requires some write ups, but all assignments are very doable and do not take up much time. Participation is graded on quantity and quality, but tbh as long as you participate and make yourself memorable in a good way, participation marks should be the easiest to get.

sections.content:
If you study with your best of your efforts, then the theories taught in class will be quite useful in your daily life, especially when getting along with people in the workplace.

See syllabus for the topics covered, not meaningful to copy-paste here.
sections.teaching:
Simply a friendly professor and lectures won't be too boring. However, explaining boring theories gets you fall asleep, so this is why she used exercise during lectures to record participation.

It's fine to skip a few lectures during project period, but better not skip those during presentation, which she cares about you coming on time.
sections.grading:
I don't think you earn "A range" with "less than average" effort put into it. Though she's friendly, her grading gets strict in the Quizzes and Report.

Chinese professors means Chinese level depth of understanding of course content. To do well in quizzes, please make sure you remember every line of text in lecture notes, and better, know how to apply these concepts in the context of Quizzes.

The presentation and report are based on a "selected target article", a list of articles she handpicked. Every group works in a different article. You compete against other groups to get your desired article. What is required in presentation and report is also different. She looks for an interesting, "easy-to-digest" presentation. But for report, she said she look for "a deep level of analysis" based on your target article. She has been using the target article for many semesters, so she knows better than you do. I suggest having different people to work on the presentation/report since the requirements are different.

All grading components are released, but quite late, like a month after you have completed the project.
sections.workload:
Fair for a 4-credit course, with 2 quizzes (during midterm period and just before final period), so it really depends on how your other courses are spread out.

In terms of project, random grouping and she said she based on "diversity" to form teams. There is one presentation and one report, split into three different parts (report written by yourself, generate report based on AI and a team evaluation report). The presentation happens during project period and reports are only submitted during study break, so it should be fine.

I think as long as you hand in the self-assessments on time, you get full marks. No attendance required except for the presentation day. There are two exams and a presentation. The two exams will test and provide you with feedback of the extent to which you understand
the key concepts and theories of leadership, and the extent to which you can apply those

sections.content: The whole course teaches knowledge around Leadership. What traits, skills the leaders possess, how's the behaviour of leaders tend to be, more relationship-motivated or task-motivated, how a leader transform their subordinates to a better person and it's important to be an ethical leader. The knowledge may be quite abstract but it's pretty easy to understand. Moreover, there are some important frameworks and concepts taught which would be tested in the exams very likely.
sections.teaching: Very good professor who often carries out class discussion and give feedback to students every lesson, sometimes the discussion occupies for more than half of the time of the class. She has a good attitude, sometimes students answer too much but she still tries her best to give helpful feedback. The teaching speed is not fast which allows students to easily catch up the concepts, she also give examples.
sections.grading:
Very good grading, didn't expect I would get an A since I got below mean in the first exam. The second exam is quite challenging because there are only 75 minutes for 4 essay questions, 13.75 marks for each question and each passage is quite long. The key to stand out in exam 2 is to be very clear with the concepts, fast reading and typing speed. Although the exam is open-book, it takes you time to locate the concepts, therefore it's important to have enough revision. Many people could not manage to finish the Exam 2 and lost mark for the final questions, I was lucky to finish it 5 minutes before the exam ended. How she graded the answers should be quite lenient since I got 54/55 in the exam.

For the project, the presentation is more important than the report, 20% and 15%. She is a good grader that she often gives high marks to groups so the mean is high, just make sure not to include significant mistakes in the Powerpoint and prepare well for the Q&A session during presentation.

Learning Diary 8% (8/8)
Self-assessment 8% (8/8)
Exam1 14% (12/14) 23/25 Mean: 23.4
Exam2 25% (24/25) 54/55 Mean: 48.2
Team Project 35% (19/20+13/15) Mean: Present 17.8 Report 12.2
Participation 10% (?/10) I guess I have like maybe 8 at least

Final Grade: A (84+?/100)

Remember to submit the learning diaries and self-assessments, those are easy-earning points which you submit and gain full mark, she seems give no mercy to those who submit late, please remember to submit.

The exams calculation is not normal, you got 1% less if you score 1 mark less in the exams. That means 55 = 25%, 54 = 24%, 52-53 = 23%, 51 = 22%, 50 = 21%...... Same calculation method for Exam 1, therefore it would be very painful for losing each mark. You can imagine in the Exam 2 not having time to do the last question will result in a disaster since the course is highly competitive (mean in Exam 1 which is MCs having mean at 23.4).

The participation marks would be calculated in two parts, first part is the attendance of the presentation classes and the guest speaker session. The other part is the class discussion, if you contribute to it then you may earn extra credits from the 10% as the syllabus said.
sections.workload:
The workload is low. Those assessments just take you little time to finish. For the revision, it may take you some time but I jotted notes each lesson so I just used little time to revise for the exams.

The big boss would be the project. I am very thankful to have very good groupmates which we all work really hard for the projects and divide the workload evenly(I think), therefore the workload is light. I myself am not a very professional in doing projects, but the teamwork we had had made us a great success in both preparing and finishing the projects, it was also a very fruitful and exciting opportunity to work with them. I would like to use this platform to say thank you to them, hope they would see it.

sections.content:
Closely related to MGMT 2110 and actually it is an extension of it.
1st half is about the leadership in individual level (e.g. OCEAN personality), while the 2nd half is about the leadership application in group level (e.g. Path-Goal Theory, Transformational Leadership etc.)
sections.teaching: Prof. Zhu is a nice professor and she is willing to engage every student in the class. She explained the concept clearly and the PPT are reader-friendly as well
sections.grading:
Assessments that are credited by hand in on time:
(Professor would not mark them)
1. Learning Diary x 3 = 15% for the course grade
2. Self-Assessment x8/9  = 10% for the course grade
Assessments that would be graded:
1. Exam 1 = 15%: 40 mark is the full mark of the exam (combination of MCs and SQ) which was conducted on Mid-March
2. Exam 2 = 20%: 60 mark is the full mark of the exam (combination of MCs and SQ) was conducted on Late-April
3. Group Project = 25%
a) Presentation = 10% + b) Final Report = 15%
4. Participation = 15%
a) Attendance for regular lesson; b) Attendance for students' presentations (3%); c) Q&A card during students' presentations

After talking about the assessments required in this course, let me talk about the statistic for this course:
Exam 1:
Mean = 32.28/40;S.D.= 3.83; Min. =15/40;Max.= 40/40
(My score is 36/40)
Exam 2:
Mean = 49.31/60;S.D. = 7.36; Max. = 59/60
(My score is 55/60)
Group presentation:

(My score is 43/45)

(My score is 49/60)
Participation:
The professor did not disclose the result yet from my observation most students have not raised questions in Q&A sessions during students' presentation (which is one common practice for HK students lol)
And I have grabbed 5 Q&A cards by actively asking questions in class
(I guess I got the most Q&A cards among all three sessions; given that I have not missed a single lesson, I think my participation should be full marked)
As a result, I got A+ in this course which I think is quite decent
